assessments.reasoning: The manual applies Initialize to a controlled object initialized by default and to controlled subcomponents without an assigned initial value. The sequencing paragraph places an object-level hook after subcomponent initialization.

challenge.method: Read §7.6(10/2,12) together with (22/2–27/2) and check the linked declaration boundary in §3.3.1.
challenge.results: The subcomponent predicate is absence of an assigned value. Access-discriminant components have additional order and allocator task activation comes after Initialize. The omission permission is conditional and an omitted Initialize cannot be user-defined. The claim explicitly confines itself to the abstract rule.

limitations: This is the manual's default-initialization rule. Paragraph 12 has additional sequencing for access-discriminant components and allocators. Paragraphs 22/2–27/2 describe an omission permission under stated conditions for nonlimited controlled objects.
Exact unannotated Ada 2022 manual edition only. Runtime implementations and other editions require separate evidence.
